cards.back: Every change is appended to a log, servers agree on the order of entries, and each applies them in that order to its own state machine. Same log, same order, same state.

For a small amount of state that must never be wrong: who the leader is, which node owns which shard, locks and cluster config. You usually use it through a system like etcd rather than implementing it.
A counter that only goes up; each term has at most one leader. Every message carries the sender's term, and a leader that sees a higher term steps down, so stale leaders are detected without clocks.
A follower that hears nothing for its election timeout (randomly about 150 to 300 ms) becomes a candidate, increments the term, votes for itself and asks the others for votes.
A server votes for at most one candidate per term, and only one whose log is at least as up to date as its own. This ensures a new leader already has every committed entry.
They make it unlikely two followers start elections at once and split the vote. If they do, both time out again at different random moments and one wins.

cards.front: When is a Raft entry committed?
cards.back: Once a majority, including the leader, stores it. Only then does the leader apply it, answer the client and advertise the new commit index.
Each AppendEntries includes the index and term of the previous entry. A follower without that entry refuses, and the leader backs up and resends until the logs match, which repairs lagging followers.
3 servers tolerate 1 failure, 5 tolerate 2. Even sizes (4 or 6) add cost without adding tolerance.
About the leader's disk fsync plus a round trip to the slowest server in the fastest majority. A millisecond or two in one region, 30 to 100 ms across three regions.
In a 2 | 3 split, only the side with 3 can elect a leader and commit. The old leader on the minority side can accept writes but never commit them, and they are overwritten when the network heals.
Election timeouts too short for GC pauses or slow fsyncs cause needless elections, each a brief write outage. Tune timeouts well above p99 heartbeat delay and use pre-vote.

quiz.q: How many failures does a 4-server Raft cluster tolerate?
choices: 1, the same as 3 servers
quiz.why: A majority of 4 is 3, so only one server can be lost.

quiz.q: A five-server cluster splits 2 | 3. What happens to writes the old leader accepts on the 2 side?
choices: They are never committed and get overwritten after healing
They commit once the split heals
They merge with the majority's writes
They are committed because the leader accepted them
quiz.why: Without a majority the old leader cannot commit; it steps down when it sees a higher term.

quiz.q: What ensures a newly elected Raft leader has every committed entry?
choices: Voters only grant votes to candidates whose log is at least as up to date
The leader copies logs from every follower after winning
Elections happen only after a snapshot
The highest server ID always wins
quiz.why: Committed entries live on a majority, and any winning candidate must satisfy one of them.

quiz.q: A three-region Raft group adds roughly what to every write?
choices: A cross-region round trip, 30 to 100 ms
Nothing, writes are local
About 1 microsecond
Several seconds
quiz.why: Commit needs a majority, which spans regions.

quiz.q: How do systems like CockroachDB and TiKV scale past one leader's capacity?
choices: Thousands of small Raft groups, one per data range
A single giant Raft group with more followers
Letting followers accept writes
Disabling fsync
quiz.why: All writes in one group go through one leader, so they shard into many groups.

quiz.q: Lose 3 of 5 servers. What does the cluster do?
choices: Stops accepting writes, by design
Keeps writing with the remaining 2
Elects two leaders
Turns into an eventually consistent store
quiz.why: Without a majority, nothing can be committed.

quiz.q: How does a far-behind follower catch up without replaying millions of entries?
choices: The leader sends it a snapshot
It becomes leader and rebuilds
It reads from a backup database
It skips the missing entries
quiz.why: Servers snapshot state and discard old log entries.
